newsitem.title: GERMANY: German motor insurers eye '96 profit, losses in 97.
newsitem.headline: German motor insurers eye '96 profit, losses in 97.

text.p: German motor insurers expect to post an underwriting profit in 1996 despite declining premiums, but predicted the industry may swing to underwriting losses next year.

Bruno Gas, head of the German property and casualty insurers' federation Verband der Schadenversicherer, told German newspaper Koelner Stadt-Anzeiger at the weekend that 1996 premium income would drop by 4.5 percent to 42.1 million marks.
The drop is expected despite a one percent rise in the number of insured vehicles, he added.
"In full comprehensive (insurance), profits will fall by 50 percent to 900 million marks, while in liability (insurance) the loss will double to 1.2 billion marks," Gas said.
Semi-comprehensive insurance is expected to post a profit of 400 million marks. He did not comment on results from passenger accident coverage.
In 1997, premium income would go down further by around 7 percent, Gas said. "Then we will certainly end up with losses."
Gas said that for the same type of car a high motor premium can now be 14 times the level of the lowest.
For a Volkswagen Golf with 60 HP, a civil servant with a 25-year no-claims bonus living in a certain regions paid 228 marks per year, Gas said.
This compares with an unemployed beginning driver who lives in another region class and pays a premium level of 245 percent a total of 3,173 marks for the same type of car, Gas said.
